checks.title: Reflow at 320px: content width ≥ 272px and largest heading ≤ 40px
The page grid fits every breakpoint: at its narrowest width each column is ≥ 40px and gutters take ≤ a third of the row
Panes add up: a pane goes inline only at a breakpoint where the main region still holds a full reading line (layout.measure.reading) and its own grid keeps columns ≥ 40px
A sticky header never hides focus: it holds its controls in every density, the scroll padding is its height, and it sticks only in windows ≥ 30em tall, where it takes ≤ 25% of the height
One set of breakpoints: rising from 0, shared by type and layout, and the same in tokens.css (em) and Tailwind (rem), so both follow the reader's text size

rules.rule: Page edges are layout.margin: the side padding of the page content (or the main region's page) uses layout.margin — the .ds-page class or px-margin. Never a spacing inset token, px, rem or vw.
rules.why: The margin follows the breakpoint and is linked to the spacing scale; the reflow check counts on it (288px of content at 320px).

rules.rule: No fixed widths on containers. Containers take max-width with a layout token (layout.container.max, layout.measure.reading, a pane width) or a fluid value; never width in px, rem or vw above the smallest screen, and never min-width that forces a wide layout.
rules.why: A 1200px box on a 320px screen scrolls 880px sideways; at 400% zoom every desktop becomes that screen.

rules.rule: Running text stays within layout.measure.reading (the .ds-measure class, max-w-reading). Never a px max-width on text, and never a width that grows with the screen.
rules.why: Past about 75 characters readers lose the next line; a px width shrinks the line at 200% text and grows it on wide screens.

rules.rule: A sticky or fixed header is layout.header.height tall (as min-height), sticks only in windows at least 30em tall (the .ds-shell header does both), and the page keeps scroll-padding-top: layout.scroll-padding.top (tokens.css sets it on <html>). Every other sticky bar adds its own height to the scroll padding. Never set scroll-padding-top to anything else.
rules.why: When the browser scrolls to a focused item or an anchor, it stops at the scroll padding — without it the item lands under the header. In short windows (400% zoom, 200% text on a laptop) a header that wraps would outgrow its padding, so there it scrolls away.

rules.rule: Grid and flex items that hold content can shrink: grid tracks are minmax(0, 1fr) (never a bare 1fr or auto for content columns) and flex children that hold text or tables get min-width: 0.
rules.why: A 1fr track never gets narrower than its longest word, URL or table, so one long value pushes the whole page sideways.

rules.rule: Layouts change only at the system breakpoints: min-width media queries at breakpoint.md, .lg and .xl in em (37.5em, 64em, 90em), or Tailwind md:, lg:, xl:. No other widths, no max-width (desktop-first) queries, no px breakpoints, no Tailwind sm: or 2xl:.
rules.why: Every breakpoint is designed and checked at its narrowest width; a 768px breakpoint creates a layout nobody checked, and px breakpoints don't move when readers enlarge text.

rules.rule: Visual order follows DOM order. Don't reorder content people read or tab through with order, row-reverse, column-reverse or grid placement; the shell keeps header, start panes, main, end panes.
rules.why: Keyboard and screen-reader users follow the DOM: a sidebar moved before the content visually but after it in the code sends focus somewhere they can't see.

rules.rule: The page never scrolls sideways. Use width: 100%, not 100vw (it includes the scrollbar); never hide overflow on <html> or <body> to mask it. A wide table scrolls inside its own container, which is focusable and named (tabindex="0" and an accessible name).
rules.why: Hiding overflow cuts content off instead of reflowing it; a scrolling region keyboard users can't focus can't be scrolled.

rules.rule: Page columns come from layout.columns and layout.gutter (.ds-grid): span columns with the .ds-span-* classes, never fixed px tracks or spans set by window media queries. Cards that wrap use the tile grid (layout.tile.min); a pane uses its pane token. Inside a pane or region the grid follows the region — never add breakpoints for it.
rules.why: Fixed tracks don't fit the next breakpoint; a grid that keeps 12 columns next to an open pane gets columns too thin for content.

rules.rule: Never redefine a layout token in app code (--ds-layout-*, --ds-breakpoint-*). Change the engine config (layout.nav, layout.aside, layout.tile, layout.panes) and build, so the change is checked.
rules.why: An overridden width skips the checks that prove panes and grids fit.

tokens.name: layout.gutter
tokens.use: Gap between the columns of the page grid (linked to Spacing)

tokens.name: layout.margin
tokens.use: Space between the screen edge and the page content; the main region's side padding (linked to Spacing)

tokens.use: Widest the page content gets: 1440 − 2 × the xl margin, so it stops growing where xl begins and wider screens get wider margins

tokens.name: layout.measure.reading
tokens.use: Widest running text gets: about 71 characters of type.body.md at any text size (34rem)

tokens.name: layout.pane.nav
tokens.use: Navigation between the product's sections; a drawer below its breakpoint. Inline from lg (≥ 1024px)

tokens.name: layout.pane.aside

tokens.name: layout.tile.min
tokens.use: Narrowest a tile gets in a tile grid (cards on a dashboard); the grid fits as many as the row holds, and one full-width tile on the smallest screens

tokens.use: Minimum height of the app header: a control plus room above and below, in every density

tokens.name: layout.scroll-padding.top
tokens.use: Space the browser keeps clear at the top when it scrolls to a focused element or an anchor: the sticky header's height, growing with the reader's text size (WCAG 2.4.11). tokens.css sets it on <html>
